headline: Negotiation is the art of reaching agreement—finding terms that work for everyone involved
universal_truth: Most things are negotiable; the skill to find mutual value creates opportunity
fun_facts: We negotiate constantly—not just in formal deals but in daily interactions
The best negotiations create value rather than just dividing it
Skilled negotiators focus on interests, not just positions
discussion_questions: How comfortable are you with negotiation?
When have you negotiated well or poorly?
What makes a negotiation feel fair?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Life is negotiation. Salary, schedules, who does dishes—we constantly work out arrangements with others. Negotiation is finding terms both can accept. It's not combat; it's collaboration.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Many people avoid negotiating. Why develop this skill?

options.text: Negotiation creates better outcomes—accepting the first offer often leaves value on the table; skilled negotiation finds solutions that work better for everyone; it's a learnable skill with high returns
options.response: Yes. The first offer isn't usually the best possible deal. Negotiation finds what's possible. It's uncomfortable but valuable—those who negotiate effectively get better outcomes across life.
It can feel that way, but good negotiation is collaborative—finding mutual benefit, not winning at someone's expense...

q1.title: Interests vs Positions
q1.script: Positions are what people say they want. Interests are why they want it. Good negotiators look past positions to underlying interests—there are often multiple ways to satisfy the same interest.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Interests vs Positions"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Creating Value
q2.script: Zero-sum thinking assumes one person's gain is another's loss. But negotiation can create value—finding options that give both parties more than they expected. Expand the pie before dividing it.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Preparation Matters
q3.script: Good negotiation requires preparation. Know what you want, what you'll accept, what you'll walk away from. Understand the other side's likely interests. Preparation beats improvisation.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Most things are negotiable. The skill to find mutual value creates opportunity. Learn to negotiate well.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 339. Tomorrow, we'll explore trading time for value—work. Until then, notice the negotiations in your daily life.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Negotiation Practice - Where Can You Do Better?
growTrack.activity: Think of an upcoming decision or agreement. What are your interests (not just position)? What might the other side's interests be? How could you find options that satisfy both? Practice preparing for a negotiation.
